                  <ns0:p n="1">1 AND Jacob dwelt in the land <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> of his fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers sojourn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ings.</ns0:note> wherein his father was a stranger, in the land of Canaan.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 These <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the generations <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) The events or occurrences which happened to <ns0:hi>Ia<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cob</ns0:hi> in his Family and issue. So that word is used, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 6. 9. and <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 3. 1. Or the word, <ns0:hi>These,</ns0:hi> may relate to what is said <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 35. 22. &c. The Genealogy of <ns0:hi>Esau</ns0:hi> being brought in by way of parenthesis, and that being finished, <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> returns to the <ns0:hi>Generations of Iacob,</ns0:hi> as his principal business, and proceeds in the History of their concerns.</ns0:note> of Jacob: Joseph being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren, and the lad was with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> placed <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> with them rather then with the sons of <ns0:hi>Leah,</ns0:hi> either to keep <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> humble: Or for <ns0:hi>Iosephs</ns0:hi> security, because the other sons retain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed the old grudge of their Mother, and were more like to en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vy, contemn, hate and abuse him; Or as an observer of their actions whom he most suspected, as the following words may seem to imply.</ns0:note>, his fathers wives: and Joseph brought unto his father their evil report <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Acquainted him with their lewd and wick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed courses to the dishonour of God and of their Family, that so his Father might apply such remedies as he thought meet.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 Now Israel loved Joseph more then all his children; because he was the son of his old age <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Being born when <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> was Ninety one years old. Such Children are commonly best beloved by their Parents, either because such are a singular blessing of God, and a more then common testimony of his favour, and a mercy least expected by them and therefore most prized; or because they have more pleasing conversation with them, and less experience of their misbehaviour, of which the elder oft times are guilty, whereby they alienate their Parents affections from them. This he gave him as a token of his special love, and of the rights of the first-born, which being justly taken from <ns0:hi>Reuben</ns0:hi> he conferred upon <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 5. 1.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more then all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Their hatred was so deep and keen, that they could not smother it, as for their own interest they should have done, but discovered it by their churlish words and carriages to him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And Joseph dreamed a dream <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Which it is probable he did not understand, for then he would never have told it to them, who, as he knew very well, were likely to make an evil construction and use of it.</ns0:note>, and he told it his brethren, and they hated him yet the more.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:36" />6 And he said unto them, Hear, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 42. 6, 9. and 43. 26. and 44. 14.</ns0:note> behold, we were binding sheaves in the field <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">A secret insinuation of the occasion of <ns0:hi>Iosephs</ns0:hi> advancement, which was from his counsel and care about the Corn of <ns0:hi>Egypt.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, and lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />right, and behold, your sheaves stood round a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">This was a posture of ministry and service, as is manifest both from Scripture and from common usage.</ns0:note>, and made obeisance to my sheaf.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And his brethren said to him, shalt thou in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />minion over us? and they hated him yet the more, for his dreams, and for his words <ns0:note n="‖" place="bottom">For his relation of his dreams, which they imputed to his arrogancy.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 And he dreamed yet another dream <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">That the repetition of the same thing, in another shape, might teach them, that the thing was both certain and very observable.</ns0:note>, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and behold, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 46. 29.</ns0:note> the Sun and the Moon <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">These were not mentioned in the first dream, because in the event, his brethren onely went at first to <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> and there worshipped him, as afterwards his father went with them. <ns0:hi>Obj.</ns0:hi> His father did not worship him in <ns0:hi>Egypt.                   <ns0:p n="10">10 And he told <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> to his father, and to his bre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thren; and his father rebuked him <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Not through anger at <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> or contempt of his dream, for it follows, he <ns0:hi>observed it,</ns0:hi> but partly lest <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> should be puffed up upon the account of his dreams, and principally, to allay the envy and hatred of his brethren.</ns0:note>, and said unto him, What <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> this dream that thou hast dreamed? shall I, and thy mother <ns0:note n="‖" place="bottom">Either 1. <ns0:hi>Rach<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">

                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And his brethren went to feed their fathers flock in Shechem <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">In the parts adjoyning to Shechem, in the lands which he had purchased there, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 33. 19.
